chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Barnet paid better than Lunceford
summary: Barnet had family money and paid Young about $50 a week more; he stayed about a year and did not record with him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What do you mean? The band was making

I guess -- I don't think he was that generous or anything, but he did pay pretty well because he didn't have to keep the lines in for himself. He had money, came from a money family. So he could -- I don't know how it worked, but I know he paid well.
How much more did you make in Barnet's band?
Oh, I guess I made about perhaps $50.00 a week more, which was a lot in those times.
How long did you play with Barnet?
I imagine -- I don't know exactly, but I imagine I was with Barnet about a year. I never did stay too long with most bands, you know.
No. Barnet had done most of the things that were popular when I went with him, like that "Cherokee" things of that sort. He had already done those. I didn't record with Barnet.
